TV.source: data/BTC.D_1d.csv (TradingView CRYPTOCAP:BTC.D); the W-SUN weekly close is the Sunday bar's close (Monday 00:00 UTC)

C2'.rule: primary C2 is the 2019 hump: C2' = max weekly close in (2020-06-30, C3)

P3'.rule: min weekly close in (P2, P2 + 8 weeks]

TVc.source: TV with index steps removed (see indexSteps and construction); equal to TV on and after the last step day

C2'.rule: primary C2 is the 2019 hump: C2' = max weekly close in (2020-06-30, C3)

P3'.rule: min weekly close in (P2, P2 + 8 weeks]

construction.rule: a day in 2014-04-01..2018-12-31 is a step when |dTV - dCMC| >= 0.75 points and dlog TOTAL2 - dlog BTCUSD >= 0.20 in the direction that moves BTC.D the way the gap does; on step days logit TVc moves by CoinMarketCap's logit change, otherwise by TradingView's
construction.cmcAlignment: CoinMarketCap's labels moved back one day (its row dated d+1 is the close of TradingView's day d), so dCMC(d) is the same market day as dTV(d); evidence in indexSteps.alignment
construction.chain: back-anchored to TV after the last step: TVc = TV on and after the last step day (2017-07-14), so the steps are removed from the history before it
construction.note: the forward chain (from TradingView's first day) is TVc shifted by the sum of the step corrections (+2.235 logit): parent 86.32-98.41 %, child 84.49-95.95 %; the 15-in-16 rule finds no waterfall in its parent (diagnostics.tvcForwardChained)
construction.caveat: back-anchoring turns TradingView's narrow-index 2016 logit moves into larger percentage moves: TVc's parent anchors read P0 86.87, P1 67.95, P2 84.70, P3 81.29 (TV: 98.41, 95.19, 97.19, 95.11)

CMC.source: data/BTCD_CMC_1d.csv (CoinMarketCap global dominance, the plan's canonical file, as built). Its row dated d is the snapshot at d 00:02 UTC, so the W-SUN weekly close is CMC's snapshot at Sunday 00:02 UTC, i.e. Saturday's close, one day before TradingView's weekly close (the Sunday-close version is diagnostics.cmcSundayClose); on a Sunday close the anchors ['P1', 'P2', 'C2', "C2'"] move

C2'.rule: primary C2 is the 2021 spike: C2' = the 2019 hump = max weekly close in (C1, 2020-06-30]

P3'.rule: min weekly close in (P2, P2 + 8 weeks]

indexSteps.nearRule: a step is within 1 week of an anchor when the step's W-SUN week is the anchor's week or the week before/after

alignment.rule: CoinMarketCap's row dated d is its snapshot at d 00:02 UTC = the close of TradingView's daily bar d-1 (TradingView labels a bar by its 00:00 UTC open); CMC's labels move back one day before the plan's same-day comparison |dTV(d) - dCMC(d)|, the step-day substitution and the chain

oneDayPrintResiduals.note: a one-day print shared by both days of a pair is only half-corrected by the plan's rule: the step day takes CoinMarketCap's move while the reverting neighbour (not a step) keeps TradingView's, so TVc keeps the step day's correction over the pair

indexSteps.rawLabelSteps: the list built on CMC's raw labels (one day late) is in diagnostics.indexStepsRawLabels
indexSteps.readingTV: on a same-market-day comparison the TV anchors within 1 week of a step are ['P3'] (on CMC's raw labels, one day late: ['P1', 'P3', 'C0']); the July-2016 bottom (P1) is not on a step: CoinMarketCap fell with TradingView in July 2016

TVc.setting: affine level map, cap 32, rule anchors

CMC.setting: affine level map, cap 32, rule anchors

TV.infeasibleNote: no path exists for 76 members (a cap below what an anchored segment needs); on the primary anchors the tightest segment puts the 89 child weeks C2..C3 on the 5 parent weeks P2..P3, so caps below 18 have no path there

TVc.infeasibleNote: no path exists for 84 members (a cap below what an anchored segment needs); on the primary anchors the tightest segment puts the 89 child weeks C2..C3 on the 4 parent weeks P2..P3, so caps below 23 have no path there

CMC.infeasibleNote: no path exists for 2 members (a cap below what an anchored segment needs); on the primary anchors the tightest segment puts the 156 child weeks C1..C2 on the 23 parent weeks P1..P2, so caps below 7 have no path there

T1.rule: share of the placed TV family members within +-4 parent weeks of the TV family median

diagnostics.note: the plan's 40 single-anchor jitters (8 anchors x offsets -2..+2) include 8 zero offsets that repeat the primary anchor set; the share without them is shown beside the verdict
diagnostics.denominatorNote: the verdict counts placed members only (188 of 264); 76 members have no feasible path; counting them as misses gives 0.667 (fragile under that plain reading of 'share of the TV family')

nullCalibration.status: labelled diagnostic beside the plan's T1 verdict
nullCalibration.design: the full TV family (264 members) placed at today's week on synthetic children: the real C0..C3 plus an open part of 285 weeks that is an 8-week block bootstrap of the child's own post-C3 logit increments (200), a logit random walk matched to their sd 0.0428 (200), or the child frozen at C3's level (1); T1 share computed as for the real child (placed members, +-4 weeks of the family median)

walk.realSharePercentileRule: mid-rank: null shares below the real share plus half of the ties

flat.realSharePercentileRule: mid-rank: null shares below the real share plus half of the ties

nullCalibration.reading: 96% of block-bootstrap children and 70% of matched walks also pass T1, so a 'robust' placement is the expected outcome under the null, not evidence that the child follows the parent

capDiagnostics.note: the anchors alone need 1.0 to 22.0 child weeks per parent week across the three anchored segments (the mapping is not one time scale); cap 16 places 12 of its 88 members (cap 32: 88 of 88; cap 64: 88 of 88); with most cap-16 members infeasible, the plan's cap robustness is largely untested at the small end; the primary anchors are infeasible at caps [8, 12, 16]; the primary placement sits on the cap floor at caps [20, 24] (capSweepPrimary)

levelLookup.childLevelRule: the highest end level (5-point grid) of the crash control whose placement lies inside the decline
levelLookup.reading: under the map the parent's open part reads 40.9-47.8% on the plateau (2016-12-25..2017-03-05), 36.0% at the first decline week (2017-03-12) and 2.5% at the low (2017-08-27); the child's open part runs 39.4-65.7% (mean 52.2%), with 64% of its weeks above the plateau's mapped maximum, so the open-end DTW parks today on the highest reachable parent weeks (the top just before the fall); the placement moves with the child's level (placement.positiveControls)

crash.design: the child's last 26 weeks replaced by a straight logit line to the given level

plantedReplica.design: the child's open part replaced by the mapped parent from P3 through week J, stretched over the open part and started at C3's level

nextWaterfall.lowRule: min weekly close in (start, start + 16 weeks], the rule's own window

local52.parkedNote: parked: the last 52 child weeks advance the path by 1 parent week (one parent week holds at most 32 child weeks, so 52 weeks need 2 columns); the clock reads 52 by construction, not from a matched shape

fixed5.coverage: fixed5 is scored on alternate weeks only (117 of the 234 T3 weeks): both source files were thinned to every 2 weeks (study8_common.thin(every=2)) with the same parity, and the second file adds 0 dates to the first (identical values on 185 common dates), so the merge reads out8 only; the common-week fractal and climatology Briers above differ from the full-window ones (fullWindowBriers)
fixed5.selection: walk-forward fits with a 26-week label lag, but the signal set was selected post hoc over refits through 2026 (round 8 note: 'a post-hoc comparator, not a pre-registered one'), so fixed5's Brier is an optimistic benchmark

TV.rule: Brier better than the expanding climatology with 26-week block-bootstrap q05 > 0 AND above the p95 of the placebo improvements (40 placebo parents per family (a)-(d), pooled; the plan's full run uses 40)
TV.note: in this window the expanding climatology averages 0.339 against a fall rate of 0.085, so a constant forecast of 0 improves on it by +0.0627; its block-bootstrap q05 is +0.0025 at 26 weeks with the module's seed and positive in 6 of 15 (block length, seed) cells (blockLengthAndSeed), and the period base rate beats the climatology by +0.0700: constant low forecasts meet or nearly meet the climatology criterion here, so the placebo p95 is the bar that decides

constantForecasts.note: the T3 window's fall rate is below the expanding climatology's, so p = 0 beats the climatology; placebo parents whose families never sit just before a waterfall score that

pShape.note: the 15-in-16 flag runs for months (see readout.<series>.waterfallCalendar), so a placed week inside it has the next rule week one week later; p(t) = 1 exactly when h(t) >= 1 (local clock <= 26) on 100% of the weeks, so p(t) is close to that indicator

episodes.note: the 26-week labels overlap, so positive weeks come in runs; the score rests on this many episodes

placeboTies.note: a placebo parent whose family is never placed within h(t) of a waterfall start has p(t) = 0 and scores the always-zero improvement exactly; when most do, the placebo p95 is the always-zero bar

episodes.note: the 26-week labels overlap, so positive weeks come in runs; the score rests on this many episodes

trailing4yClimatology.rule: mean of fall5_26w over the 208 labelled weeks known at t

placeboTies.note: a placebo parent whose family is never placed within h(t) of a waterfall start has p(t) = 0 and scores the always-zero improvement exactly; when most do, the placebo p95 is the always-zero bar

CMC.constantLowForecastNote: in this window the expanding climatology averages 0.339 against a fall rate of 0.085, so a constant forecast of 0 improves on it by +0.0627; its block-bootstrap q05 is +0.0025 at 26 weeks with the module's seed and positive in 6 of 15 (block length, seed) cells (blockLengthAndSeed), and the period base rate beats the climatology by +0.0700: constant low forecasts meet or nearly meet the climatology criterion here, so the placebo p95 is the bar that decides
CMC.aucNote: AUC 0.345 < 0.5: p(t) ranks the fall weeks below the non-fall weeks (anti-predictive)

tvcForwardChained.status: labelled diagnostic: TVc chained forward from TradingView's first day (2014-04-01) on the aligned step list; the first build chained forward on CMC's raw labels; the plan's TVc (main results) is back-anchored
tvcForwardChained.why: forward chaining puts TVc at 86.32-98.41 % in the parent and 84.49-95.95 % in the child (today 93.47 %); the parent's largest fall within 16 weeks is 11.78 points, so the 15-in-16 rule finds no waterfall in its parent: no read-out, p(t) = 0, and the shape members' open-part normalisation runs to the parent end. The first build's TVc T1 'fragile' and p(t) = 0 were artefacts of this chaining, not of the data; affine placements do not depend on it (a constant logit shift goes into the intercept)

cmcSundayClose.status: labelled diagnostic: CMC's labels moved back one day, so its W-SUN weekly close is the snapshot at Monday 00:02 UTC (Sunday's close, as TradingView's); the plan's CMC rerun uses the canonical file as built (Saturday's close)

placementBaseRate.status: labelled diagnostic beside the plan, not a verdict input
placementBaseRate.design: 200 logit random walks matched to the child's post-C3 weekly increment sd (0.0428), starting at C3's level, 285 weeks, and 200 8-week block bootstraps of the child's own post-C3 increments; each child = the real C0..C3 plus the synthetic open part, placed with the primary setting (TV parent, rule anchors, affine, cap 32); the same children feed placement.T1.nullCalibration

classes.decline: the first decline week through the episode low (2017-08-27)

within4WeeksCriterion.note: the 15-in-16 flag runs for months, so 'within 4 parent weeks before the next waterfall' holds on 28 of the 50 placeable weeks, from the plateau into the decline; synthetic children meet it in 100% (block) and 100% (walk), so it carries little information (kept for continuity; the class shares above replace it)

capFloor.rule: with 286 child weeks C3..today and at most 32 child weeks on one parent week, the open-end placement cannot come earlier than P3 + 8 weeks

placementBaseRate.verdictOnMethod: block bootstraps of the child's own increments land on the plateau in 91% and inside the decline in 9%; matched walks 49% / 51%; a uniform placement over the reachable weeks 9% / 58%. The real placement (plateau) is the typical outcome for children with the child's own increments: it reflects the child's level against the mapped parent (placement.levelLookup), not evidence that the child follows the parent's shape

zigzagWaterfallsOnTVParent.rule: study.py waterfalls(): zigzag 6-point reversals, falls >= 15 points, start when 15% of the depth is done

clockToMatchTops.note: the child's 2025-06-22 top matched to the parent's 2017-02-26 top since (P3, C3)

shapeVariantPrimary.note: the parent's open part is z-scored over (P3, start of the parent's 2017 waterfall], the start by the 15-in-16 rule (at least 4 weeks); the plan wrote (P3, 2017-03-05] expecting the rule's start there, but the rule fires earlier (see diagnostics.shapeLiteralWindow)

shapeLiteralWindow.status: labelled diagnostic: the TV family's shape members with the parent's open part z-scored over the plan's literal window (P3, 2017-03-05] instead of (P3, first rule week]

truncationTest.what: rows: the primary and shape-primary members' placement and the local clock at t, full forward pass vs a run on the child cut at t; familyRows: the whole TV family cut at t (every placement, h(t) and p(t), including the weeks either side of the C3' members' entry); placeboNoiseTest: one placebo walk-forward rerun with the child after a cut replaced by noise, p(t) compared up to the cut

climatology.rule: expanding mean of TV fall5_26w over weeks s <= t - 26 (labels known at t), from 2014-04

leakage.anchors: hindsight by design: the anchors (and C2', P3', the jitters) are fixed from the full history; every primary anchor window closes before T3 starts (C3's on 2021-06-30; T3 starts at C3 + 26 weeks). C3' (min weekly close in 2021-07-01..2022-06-30) is the only anchor whose window overlaps T3 (33 weeks): its members are placed only from 2022-07-03, once the window has closed, in the real families and in every placebo walk-forward (measured effect in leakage.c3PrimeTiming)

parentEnd.rule: every real member's parent ends at or before the primary C0 - 1 week (2017-12-03 on TV): a C0 jitter's parent ends at min(its own C0 - 1, the primary C0 - 1), so no parent contains a child week

leakage.openPart: at child week t only child data up to t enters the open part, the local clock (52 child weeks back along the path ending at t) and the shape variant's child normalisation (C3, t]; the anchored part uses child weeks <= C3 < t

fixed5.note: fixed5 probabilities read from the out-of-sample files only; compared on common weeks
fixed5.selection: walk-forward fits with a 26-week label lag, but the signal set was selected post hoc over refits through 2026 (round 8 note), so fixed5's Brier is an optimistic benchmark; it is a reported comparator, not in the T3 pass rule

leakage.t2Search: the T2 anchor search scores only the anchored part (child C0..C3); the open part never enters the search

multipleComparisons.t2FamiliesNeeded: 4 of 5 (a)-(e), plus (f) worse than the real parent
multipleComparisons.reruns: TVc and CMC are reported beside TV and never rescue a TV fail
multipleComparisons.crossRound: round 14 in a sequence of studies on the same TradingView BTC.D history: rounds 1-7 and 11 tested fractal alignments of 2016-17 onto 2018-now, rounds 8-10, 12 and 13 other forecasters and patterns; Steven revised this mapping after seeing round 11's chart
forkingPaths: the T1 denominator (placed members for the verdict; all members in placement.T1.diagnostics)
the TVc construction (CMC alignment and chain anchor; indexSteps, diagnostics.tvcForwardChained)
how the waterfall start is read (the 15-in-16 rule fires weeks before the top; readout.<series>.waterfallCalendar)
the shape variant's open-part normalisation window (diagnostics.shapeLiteralWindow)
multipleComparisons.nTestResultsReported: 9 (3 series x 3 tests), plus labelled diagnostics
multipleComparisons.note: three tests on one verdict series; no correction beyond the pre-registered thresholds. Neither evidence test (T2 shape, T3 forecast) passes, so no correction would change those verdicts; T1 is a robustness reading, not a test against chance (placement.T1.nullCalibration). A future pass would need a correction across rounds and across the choices in forkingPaths

notes: Weekly = W-SUN last close of complete weeks: the daily files end 2026-11-02, so the week ending 2026-11-08 (BTC.D 60.35 so far) is partial and excluded; today's child week is 2026-11-01 (BTC.D 60.50).
Anchors are the plan's rules on each series' weekly closes; P0/C0 use the 8 weeks before P1/C1; ties go to the earliest week.

TVc compares TradingView's day d with CoinMarketCap's change over the same market day: CMC's row dated d is its 00:02 UTC snapshot (the close of TradingView's bar d-1), so its labels move back one day before the step rule (indexSteps.alignment). TVc is back-anchored: TVc = TV on and after the last step day (2017-07-14); the forward chain from 2014-04-01 is TVc + 2.235 logit and is a labelled diagnostic (diagnostics.tvcForwardChained), as is the first build's step list on CMC's raw labels (11 days; diagnostics.indexStepsRawLabels).

On the forward chain the TVc family reads T1 fragile (0.5172) and the 15-in-16 rule finds no waterfall in its parent, so the first build's TVc 'fragile' and p(t) = 0 were a chaining artefact, not a property of the data (diagnostics.tvcForwardChained)
CMC (the plan's canonical file, as built) closes its W-SUN week on Saturday (its Sunday 00:02 UTC snapshot); the Sunday-close version is diagnostics.cmcSundayClose.

DTW cells: child week i matched to parent week j; moves child+1 / parent+1 / both; at most `cap` child weeks on one parent week; a parent-only step adds the penalty lambda; the path is forced through the four anchor cells (diagonal moves that would skip a corner are forbidden); lambda = median squared residual of the anchored part's path computed with that lambda (fixed point).

The open end may place today anywhere in (P3, parent end]; the parent end is C0 - 1 week (2017-12-03 on TV); a C0 jitter's parent ends at min(its own C0 - 1, the primary C0 - 1), so no parent contains a child week.

Family members with no feasible path (a cap too small for a segment) are reported and left out of the quantiles; T1's verdict counts placed members only, and the share counting them as misses is shown beside it (verdicts.placementDiagnostics).

T1 under the null: 96% of block-bootstrap children and 70% of matched-walk children pass it (placement.T1.nullCalibration), so a robust T1 is the expected outcome under the null; the placement tracks the child's level against the mapped parent (placement.levelLookup, placement.positiveControls).

T2 search: P1 among the 3 deepest local minima in the window's first 30 weeks, P0 = max of the 8 weeks before P1 (inside the window), P2 among the 3 highest local maxima within 30 weeks after P1, P3 = min of the 4 weeks after P2; lowest anchored cost wins.

T2 surrogates (a)-(c) are built on the series' weekly logit 2014-04..parent end and cut at the parent's calendar positions; (b) is study.py block_shuffle (8-week blocks of increments, permuted); (d) every weekly start 2014-04..2016-04; (e) every window of the parent's length that ends by the parent end (no overlap with the child), spread evenly to the placebo count.

T3: p(t) = share of the placed TV family members whose placed week is within h(t) = 26 / local clock(t) parent weeks before their next waterfall start (the first later week with a 15-point fall inside 16 weeks); members whose C3 is after t are not placed, and the C3' members (window 2021-07-01..2022-06-30) are placed only once the window has closed, in the real families and in every placebo walk-forward (leakage.c3PrimeTiming).
T3 placebo walk-forwards search their anchors once (anchored part, child C0..C3) and then run the same family and walk-forward.

T3 pass needs the improvement strictly above the pooled placebo p95 (160 parents, (a)-(d)); a placebo whose p(t) is 0 every week scores the always-zero improvement, so a real p(t) = 0 ties that p95 and does not pass.

The shape variant z-scores the parent's open part over (P3, W], W = the first week after P3 from which the parent falls 15 points within 16 weeks (the plan's waterfall rule; at least 4 weeks after P3; the parent end when no week qualifies). This departs from the plan's literal (P3, 2017-03-05] on TV: the plan named that date as the expected start of the parent's 2017 waterfall, but the rule fires weeks before the top, so the window as built is shorter; the rule is kept because it applies to every series and placebo parent, and the literal window's result is diagnostics.shapeLiteralWindow.

The 15-in-16 flag runs for months on the TV parent, so 'the next waterfall start' is one week after any placement inside that run, including placements inside the decline; readout.<series>.waterfallCalendar classifies the placed week (plateau / decline / later).
